title: Left Hand
cues: Seven-ten every mornin', you lean in to the sink
Pale porcelain sink, a single dripping faucet, shadows lengthen
build
I lean in too, just a little slower than you think
A hand mirrors another, slow, deliberate, distorted reflections
build
You brush with your right, so I brush with my left
Silver brushes against tarnished metal, a ghostly exchange
build
You spit, I spit, and you never smell my breath
A choked cough, a dark stain blooming on white cloth
build
Forty-four years of your faces, I could draw 'em with no light
Dozens of faded portraits, spectral faces in a dim gallery
build
The funeral face, the payday face, the face you make at night
A skeletal face in a cracked mirror, a shadowed, expectant gaze
drive
You practiced "I love you" on me 'fore you said it out loud
A lone, antique harpsichord keys slowly descend into darkness
drive
You practiced cryin' too. I was better. You'd be proud
Tears suspended in the air, shimmering like captured light
drive
Every lie you ever told, I heard it first, rehearsed
A warped music box spins, playing a fractured, unsettling tune
drive
You'd try it on in the glass, and I would mouth it in reverse
A hand mimics a gesture, reversed, a dark reflection back
drive
I'm your left hand
A skeletal hand reaching out, a cold, silent grasp
drive
Been your left hand all your life
A dark silhouette against a frosted window, a lonely presence
drive
You ever wonder what I do when you flip off the light?
Darkness, a figure stands motionless in a vacant room
drive
I stay standin' in the dark and keep my face polite
A lone hand reaching for a reflective surface, cold and still
drive
You ever leave the bathroom and swear the glass was slow to clear?
A fractured mirror, distorted glass reflecting an empty space
drive
That's me, finishin' a thought you didn't want to hear
A silent, thoughtful face in a darkened doorway, contemplation
drive
Your scar is on my right side, and your watch is on the wrong wrist
A tarnished watch lies on a cold surface, a missing hand
drive
Your ring is on my other hand, so tell me who she kissed
A hand cradles a ring, a haunting, unanswered question
drive
When your wife leans in behind you, fixin' lipstick in the glass
A woman’s reflection, a fleeting smile, in a darkened mirror
drive
Who you think she's smilin' at? Go 'head. Think about it. Ask
A dark space, a question mark hanging in the air
drive
Your mama hung a sheet on me the week your daddy passed
A sheet hangs over a ghostly form, a silent vigil
drive
Said the dead get turned around in a house with naked glass
Cracked glass reflecting a distorted, unsettling image
drive
Seven nights under that sheet, and guess who came and sat
A shadowed figure sits, observing with a vacant stare
drive
Your daddy, lost and lookin', and I told him where you're at
A pointed finger, a dark knowing, a chilling direction
drive
I'm your left hand
A skeletal hand reaching out, a cold, silent grasp
drive
Been your left hand all your life
A dark silhouette against a frosted window, a lonely presence
drive
It's Halloween
A swirling mist, reflections of faces shift and distort
drive
Glass gets thin tonight
Thin, fragile glass, a shimmering, dangerous surface
drive
Everybody on your street is wearin' somebody else's face
Silhouettes wearing faces, moving silently through the dark
build
So nobody's gonna notice
An unseen hand waves, lost in the infinite darkness
build
When you wave
A hand falls still, suspended in the void
build
And I don't
Empty space, a dark stillness, a silent, final gesture
drive
Go on, lift your right. Let's see who moves first
A hand slowly rises, a deliberate, unsettling movement
drive
Forty-four years I been livin' your life backwards, rehearsed
A lifetime of echoes, a reversed, distorted memory
drive
You blink, I don't. You smile, I let it fade
A blank stare, a vacant acceptance, a fading recollection
drive
You step back from the sink, and I step out of the shade
A figure steps into the shadows, a slow, deliberate advance
drive
Now you're the one in the glass with the toothbrush in the wrong fist
A hand gripping a toothbrush, a distorted reflection stares back
drive
Half a second late on every move, and every move you missed
Lost seconds, a ripple in the darkness, a missed opportunity
drive
Your wife comes in behind me, and she smiles, and she don't see
A smiling woman, a blank, unfocused gaze, passing through
drive
That the man she's smilin' at ain't you no more. It's me
A cold, knowing smile, the realization of a dark truth
drive
Tomorrow at seven-ten I'll lean in to the sink
Pale porcelain sink, a single dripping faucet, shadows lengthen
drive
And you'll lean in too, just a little slower than you think
A mirrored hand, slow and deliberate, awaiting the return
drive
Now you're my left hand
Pale, skeletal hand slowly circles a rusted music box, gears frozen
build
And I'll be right
A shadowy figure extends a right hand, mirroring the movement
